title: RN-D: Discretized Categorical Actors for On-Policy Reinforcement Learning
claim: Swapping in our actor representation consistently speeds convergence and raises final performance across multiple algorithms and benchmarks over the standard baseline.
layout: 6 panels in 2x3 grid; columns are algorithms, rows are benchmarks; shared legend below
description: A 2x3 grid of line plots comparing two training curves per panel. The columns are PPO, TRPO and SPO. The top row is Gym locomotion with 5 tasks, with normalized return on the y-axis and environment steps up to 5×10^6 on the x-axis. The bottom row is ManiSkill manipulation with 10 tasks, with success rate on the y-axis and steps up to 5×10^7 on the x-axis. Each panel has an orange curve for the MLP-C baseline and a purple curve for RN-D (Ours), each with a translucent shaded variance band. The purple curve rises faster and ends higher in every panel. The gap is largest in the ManiSkill TRPO and SPO panels, where the orange baseline stays flat or plateaus. A single shared legend sits at the bottom center.
caption: RN-D consistently improve on-policy RL across algorithms. We compare the dominant standard implementation, a continuous MLP actor (MLP-C), with our regularized discretized actor (RN-D) under PPO, TRPO, and SPO on Gym locomotion and ManiSkill manipulation benchmarks. RN-D achieves faster convergence and higher final performance across both algorithms and benchmarks.
abstract: On-policy Reinforcement Learning (RL) remains a dominant paradigm for continuous control, yet standard implementations rely on Gaussian actors and relatively shallow MLP policies, often leading to brittle optimization when gradients are noisy, and policy updates must be conservative. In this paper, we revisit actor policy representation as a first-class design choice for on-policy RL. We study discretized categorical actors, which represent each action dimension as a distribution over discrete bins and induce a policy objective analogous to classification cross-entropy loss. Building on architectural advances from supervised learning, we further pair discretized categorical actors with regularized networks, yielding RN-D. Across diverse continuous-control benchmarks, we show that simply replacing the standard Gaussian actor with our proposed actor substantially improves performance, achieving state-of-the-art results within on-policy RL. We release our code at https://github.com/alwaysbyx/RND-RL.
